topics.title: 1.1 Cell Membrane & Fluid Mosaic Architecture
topics.readContent:
Module 1: Biology • Chapter 1

1.1 Cell Membrane & Fluid Mosaic Dynamics

Summary: Covers Singer & Nicolson's Fluid Mosaic Model, lipid bilayer composition, integral vs peripheral proteins, cholesterol fluidity buffer, and transport mechanisms.

1. Molecular Architecture of Biological Membranes

According to the Fluid Mosaic Model (Singer & Nicolson, 1972), biological membranes behave as a quasi-fluid two-dimensional liquid wherein amphipathic phospholipids and proteins are in continuous lateral motion.

  • Phospholipid Bilayer: Hydrophilic polar heads face aqueous environments; hydrophobic non-polar fatty acid tails sequester inward.
  • Cholesterol (Animal Cells): Acts as a biophysical fluidity buffer. It prevents crystallized packing at cold temperatures and stabilizes excess fluidity at elevated temperatures.
  • Glycocalyx: Surface oligosaccharide chains linked to lipids (glycolipids) or proteins (glycoproteins) enabling cell-cell recognition and immune identity.

topics.title: Topic 1.1 Quick Quiz: Membrane Transport & Channels

quizData.title: Topic 1.1 Checkpoint: Cell Membrane & Transport Quiz
quizData.subtitle: 5 Rapid-Fire PMDC MCQs covering active transport, passive diffusion & tonicity

questions.question: Which component of the plasma membrane acts as a fluidity buffer across temperature fluctuations in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Cholesterol prevents phospholipid fatty acid chains from packing closely at low temperatures and restricts excessive membrane fluidity at high temperatures, functioning as a biophysical fluidity buffer.

questions.question: In the Sodium-Potassium ATPase pump, what is the stoichiometric exchange ratio per ATP hydrolyzed?
questions.explanation: The primary active Na+/K+ ATPase pumps 3 Sodium ions OUT of the cell and 2 Potassium ions INTO the cell per ATP molecule cleaved, maintaining negative resting membrane potential.

questions.question: Which of the following transport mechanisms moves substances against their electrochemical gradient without direct ATP hydrolysis?
questions.explanation: Secondary active transport couples the downhill movement of an ion (such as Na+) down its gradient to drive the uphill transport of another solute against its concentration gradient.

questions.question: A red blood cell placed in a 0.2% NaCl solution will undergo:
questions.explanation: Normal physiological saline is 0.9% NaCl (isotonic). A 0.2% NaCl solution is hypotonic, causing water to rush into the erythrocyte via osmosis, leading to swelling and membrane bursting (hemolysis).

questions.question: The 'glycocalyx' found on the external surface of the plasma membrane is primarily composed of:
questions.explanation: The glycocalyx consists of carbohydrates covalently linked to membrane proteins (glycoproteins) and lipids (glycolipids), providing cell-cell recognition and immunological markers.

topics.title: 1.2 Endomembrane System & Mitochondria
topics.readContent:
Module 1: Biology • Chapter 1

1.2 Endomembrane System & Mitochondria

1. Eukaryotic Organelles Overview

Detailed analysis of mitochondria (double membrane, cristae, circular DNA, 70S ribosomes), endoplasmic reticulum (RER protein synthesis vs SER lipid synthesis & drug detox), and lysosomes (acid hydrolases with pH 4.5-5.0).

quizData.title: Chapter 1: Cell Biology & Cytology Comprehensive Exam
quizData.subtitle: PMDC standard chapter-ending evaluation covering organelles, division, and membrane dynamics.

questions.question: Crossing over between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes occurs during which specific stage of Prophase I?
questions.explanation: Synapsis occurs during Zygotene, but genetic exchange (crossing over) takes place during Pachytene via recombination nodules, producing chiasmata visible in Diplotene.

questions.question: Which organelle is directly responsible for the synthesis of steroid hormones in Leydig and adrenal cortex cells?
questions.explanation: The Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER) is enriched with enzymes for lipid and steroid biosynthesis, as well as glycogen breakdown and detoxification in hepatocytes.

questions.question: In eukaryotic ribosomes, the peptidyl transferase ribozyme activity that forms peptide bonds is located in:
questions.explanation: The catalytic peptidyl transferase activity of eukaryotic 80S ribosomes resides within the 28S ribosomal RNA of the large (60S) subunit.

questions.question: Tay-Sachs disease results from the genetic deficiency of Hexosaminidase A within which organelle?
questions.explanation: Tay-Sachs is an autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disease resulting in abnormal accumulation of GM2 gangliosides in neuronal lysosomes.

questions.question: Colchicine arrests cells in which mitotic phase by inhibiting microtubule polymerization?
questions.explanation: Colchicine disrupts mitotic spindle microtubule assembly, arresting chromosomes on the metaphase plate (used clinically for karyotyping).

topics.title: 2.1 Carbohydrate Chemistry, Isomerism & Glycosidic Bonds
topics.readContent:
Module 1: Biology • Chapter 2

2.1 Carbohydrate Chemistry & Glycosidic Linkages

Detailed study of aldoses, ketoses, hemiacetals, anomeric carbons, and classification into monosaccharides, disaccharides, and polysaccharides.

topics.title: Topic 2.1 Quick Quiz: Carbohydrate Structure & Tests

quizData.title: Carbohydrate Classification & Biochemical Tests
quizData.subtitle: 5 Rapid-Fire PMDC MCQs covering mono-, di- and polysaccharides

questions.question: Which of the following carbohydrates is a non-reducing disaccharide with an alpha-1,2-glycosidic linkage?
questions.explanation: In sucrose, both anomeric carbons of glucose and fructose participate in the glycosidic bond (alpha-1,2), leaving no free hemiacetal group; thus it does not reduce Benedict's reagent.

questions.question: Which branched polymer of glucose serves as the primary animal storage carbohydrate?
questions.explanation: Glycogen has alpha-1,4 glycosidic bonds in chains with frequent alpha-1,6 branch points occurring every 8-12 glucose residues, stored in liver and skeletal muscles.

questions.question: A patient's urine turns brick-red when heated with Benedict's solution. Which sugar is NOT responsible?
questions.explanation: Sucrose is non-reducing and gives a negative Benedict's test unless previously hydrolyzed by acid or sucrase.

questions.question: Chitin, found in fungal cell walls and arthropod exoskeletons, is a polymer of:
questions.explanation: Chitin is a homopolymer of N-acetyl-D-glucosamine units joined by beta-1,4-glycosidic linkages.

questions.question: Amylose and amylopectin are the two structural constituents of:
questions.explanation: Plant starch consists of unbranched helical amylose (alpha-1,4) and branched amylopectin (alpha-1,4 with alpha-1,6 branches).

topics.title: 2.2 Protein Hierarchy & Hemoglobin vs Myoglobin
topics.readContent:
Module 1: Biology • Chapter 2

2.2 Protein Hierarchy & Hemoglobin vs Myoglobin

Primary, secondary (alpha-helix, beta-sheet), tertiary, and quaternary levels of protein structure, with clinical comparisons of myoglobin (hyperbolic curve) and hemoglobin (sigmoidal cooperative curve).

topics.title: 2.3 Enzyme Kinetics, Michaelis-Menten & Inhibition Models
topics.readContent:
Module 1: Biology • Chapter 2

2.3 Enzyme Kinetics & Inhibition Models

Km (substrate concentration at 1/2 Vmax), competitive vs non-competitive vs uncompetitive inhibitors, and regulatory allosteric effectors.

quizData.title: Chapter 2: Biochemistry & Enzymology Comprehensive Exam
quizData.subtitle: PMDC standard assessment on amino acids, proteins, lipids, and catalytic kinetics.

questions.question: A competitive enzyme inhibitor produces which of the following kinetic alterations on Km and Vmax?
questions.explanation: Competitive inhibitors compete with substrate for active sites, requiring higher substrate concentrations to reach half-maximal velocity (increased Km), but high [S] can still achieve maximal rate (unchanged Vmax).

questions.question: Which amino acid possesses an indole ring and serves as precursor to serotonin and melatonin?
questions.explanation: Tryptophan contains an indole ring and is the biochemical precursor for neurotransmitter serotonin (5-HT) and hormone melatonin.

questions.question: Which of the following bonds stabilizes the alpha-helix secondary structure of proteins?
options: Hydrogen bonds between C=O and N-H of peptide backbones
Ionic bonds between acidic and basic side chains
questions.explanation: Alpha-helices and beta-sheets are stabilized strictly by intrachain hydrogen bonds between the carbonyl oxygen (C=O) and amide hydrogen (N-H) of the peptide backbone 4 residues apart.

questions.question: Prosthetic groups differ from coenzymes in that prosthetic groups are:
options: Permanently and tightly/covalently bound to the apoenzyme
Inorganic metal ions only (e.g., Fe2+, Mg2+)
Always synthesized de novo during every reaction cycle
questions.explanation: A prosthetic group (like heme in catalase or hemoglobin) remains tightly or covalently bound to the enzyme throughout the catalytic cycle.

questions.question: The quaternary structure of adult Hemoglobin (HbA) consists of:
options: Two alpha and two gamma globin chains
Two alpha and two beta globin chains
Single polypeptide with one heme pocket
questions.explanation: Normal adult human hemoglobin (HbA) is a tetramer of two alpha (alpha) and two beta (beta) subunits, each containing a protoporphyrin IX heme ring.

3.1 Mendelian Genetics & Inheritance Patterns

resources.name: Genetics Punnett Squares & Pedigree Analysis — PDF

topics.title: Topic 3.1 Quick Quiz: Mendelian Ratios & Pedigrees

quizData.title: Genetics & Inheritance Patterns Quiz
quizData.subtitle: 5 Rapid-Fire PMDC MCQs covering monohybrid, dihybrid, and sex-linked traits

questions.question: In a cross between two individuals heterozygous for two unlinked traits (AaBb x AaBb), what fraction of offspring is expected to express both recessive phenotypes (aabb)?
questions.explanation: Standard Mendelian dihybrid phenotypic ratio is 9:3:3:1. The double recessive phenotype (aabb) represents 1 out of 16 offspring.

questions.question: Hemophilia A is an X-linked recessive disorder. If a carrier female marries an unaffected male, what percentage of their male children will have hemophilia?
questions.explanation: The mother is X^H X^h and father is X^H Y. Male children inherit Y from father and either X^H (unaffected, 50%) or X^h (affected, 50%) from mother.

questions.question: The phenomenon where a single gene influences multiple unrelated phenotypic traits is called:
questions.explanation: Pleiotropy describes a single gene mutation producing multiple phenotypic effects across distinct organ systems (e.g., Sickle Cell Anemia, Marfan syndrome).

questions.question: During DNA replication in E. coli, which enzyme unwinds the double helix at the replication fork?
questions.explanation: DNA Helicase unwinds the double helix at the fork by breaking hydrogen bonds, while Topoisomerase (gyrase) relieves supercoiling tension ahead of the fork.

questions.question: Okazaki fragments are synthesized along the:
options: Leading strand continuously in 5' to 3' direction
Lagging strand discontinuously in 5' to 3' direction
Lagging strand continuously in 3' to 5' direction
Both strands simultaneously by RNA polymerase
questions.explanation: Because DNA polymerases only synthesize in the 5' to 3' direction, the lagging strand is synthesized discontinuously as short Okazaki fragments, later joined by DNA ligase.

quizData.title: Chapter 3: Genetics & Molecular Biology Comprehensive Exam
quizData.subtitle: PMDC standard assessment on DNA replication, transcription, translation, and genetic disorders.

questions.question: The genetic codon AUG encodes which amino acid and functions as what in eukaryotic translation?
questions.explanation: AUG codes for Methionine (Met) in eukaryotes and serves as the universal initiator (start) codon for protein translation.

questions.question: Which of the following codons does NOT code for any amino acid and acts as a translation termination signal?
questions.explanation: UAA (Ochre), UAG (Amber), and UGA (Opal) are non-sense stop codons recognized by release factors rather than tRNAs.

questions.question: In eukaryotic mRNA post-transcriptional processing, the 5' cap is composed of:
questions.explanation: Eukaryotic pre-mRNA is capped at its 5' end with 7-methylguanosine via an unusual 5'-to-5' triphosphate bridge.

questions.question: Which enzyme is responsible for synthesizing ribosomal RNA (28S, 18S, and 5.8S) in eukaryotic nucleoli?
questions.explanation: RNA Pol I transcribes major rRNAs (28S, 18S, 5.8S); RNA Pol II transcribes mRNA and snRNA; RNA Pol III transcribes tRNA and 5S rRNA.

questions.question: A cross between a red flower (RR) and white flower (WW) yielding 100% pink flowers (RW) exemplifies:
questions.explanation: Incomplete dominance occurs when heterozygotes exhibit an intermediate blended phenotype.

topics.title: 1.1 VSEPR Theory, Molecular Shapes & Bond Angles
topics.readContent:
Module 2: Chemistry • Chapter 1

1.1 VSEPR Theory & Hybridization

Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion theory: lone pair-lone pair > lone pair-bond pair > bond pair-bond pair repulsion.

topics.title: Topic 1.1 Quick Quiz: Hybridization & Bond Angles

quizData.title: Chemical Bonding & Hybridization Quiz
quizData.subtitle: 5 Rapid-Fire PMDC MCQs covering sp3, sp2, sp hybridization and geometries

questions.question: What is the hybridization state and molecular geometry of Xenon Tetrafluoride (XeF4)?
questions.explanation: Xe has 8 valence electrons + 4 F bonds = 12 electrons (6 pairs: 4 bonding pairs + 2 lone pairs). Steric number 6 = sp3d2, with lone pairs axial yielding a square planar geometry.

questions.question: According to VSEPR theory, the bond angle in a water (H2O) molecule is reduced from 109.5° to 104.5° primarily due to:
questions.explanation: The two lone pairs on oxygen exert greater repulsive forces than bond pairs, compressing the H-O-H angle from 109.5° to approximately 104.5°.

questions.question: Which of the following molecules has a net dipole moment of ZERO despite containing polar bonds?
questions.explanation: BF3 has a symmetrical trigonal planar geometry (120° angles), causing the three polar B-F bond dipoles to cancel each other out completely.

questions.question: The percentage of s-character in sp2 hybrid orbitals is:
questions.explanation: An sp2 orbital is formed by 1 s orbital and 2 p orbitals (total 3), giving 1/3 = 33.33% s-character.

questions.question: Which of the following compounds exhibits intramolecular hydrogen bonding?
questions.explanation: In o-nitrophenol, the -OH group and -NO2 group are adjacent on the benzene ring, forming an internal 6-membered hydrogen-bonded ring.

topics.title: 1.2 Intermolecular Forces & Dipole Moments
topics.readContent:
Module 2: Chemistry • Chapter 1

1.2 Intermolecular Forces & Dipole Moments

London dispersion forces, dipole-dipole attractions, hydrogen bonding, and their impact on boiling points and vapor pressures.

quizData.title: Chapter 1: Chemical Bonding Comprehensive Assessment
quizData.subtitle: PMDC standard evaluation on hybridization, geometry, and polarity.

questions.question: In ethyne (acetylene, C2H2), the carbon-carbon triple bond consists of:
options: One sigma bond and two pi bonds
Two sigma bonds and one pi bond
questions.explanation: A triple bond is composed of one axial sigma bond formed by sp-sp overlap and two lateral pi bonds formed by unhybridized 2py and 2pz orbitals.

questions.question: Which molecule has an octahedral electron-group geometry with 90° bond angles throughout?
questions.explanation: SF6 has 6 bonding pairs and 0 lone pairs around sulfur (sp3d2), giving a regular octahedral geometry with all 90° bond angles.

questions.question: Which halogen forms the strongest hydrogen bond due to highest electronegativity?
questions.explanation: Fluorine has the highest electronegativity (4.0 on Pauling scale), producing the strongest dipole and hydrogen bond in H-F.

questions.question: The bond order of Oxygen molecule (O2) according to Molecular Orbital Theory (MOT) is:
questions.explanation: O2 has 10 bonding electrons and 6 anti-bonding electrons: (10 - 6) / 2 = 2. It is paramagnetic due to two unpaired electrons.

questions.question: Coordinate covalent (dative) bonding is present in which of the following species?
questions.explanation: In NH4+, the lone pair on ammonia's nitrogen is donated to an empty 1s orbital of H+, forming a coordinate covalent bond.

Module 2: Chemistry • Chapter 2

2.1 Organic Chemistry Fundamentals

topics.title: Topic 2.1 Quick Quiz: Organic Reaction Intermediates

quizData.title: Organic Chemistry Checkpoint Quiz
quizData.subtitle: 5 Rapid-Fire PMDC MCQs covering carbocations, isomerism & Markovnikov addition

questions.question: Which of the following carbocations is thermodynamically the most stable?
questions.explanation: Tertiary (3°) carbocations are stabilized by hyperconjugation (9 alpha-hydrogens in tert-butyl) and +I inductive electron donation.

questions.question: Addition of HBr to propene in the absence of peroxides yields 2-bromopropane as major product according to:
questions.explanation: Markovnikov's rule states that the electrophilic H+ adds to the carbon with more hydrogen atoms to generate the more stable secondary carbocation intermediate.

questions.question: How many structural isomers exist for pentane (C5H12)?
questions.explanation: C5H12 has exactly 3 structural isomers: n-pentane, isopentane (2-methylbutane), and neopentane (2,2-dimethylpropane).

questions.question: Benzene undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution rather than addition primarily because substitution:
options: Preserves the stable aromatic sextet resonance
questions.explanation: Addition would destroy the 36 kcal/mol resonance stabilization energy of the delocalized aromatic pi-ring.

questions.question: Which compound exhibits geometrical (cis-trans) isomerism?
questions.explanation: But-2-ene has two different groups (H and CH3) attached to each double-bonded carbon, allowing cis- and trans- stereoisomers.

quizData.title: Chapter 2: Organic Chemistry Mastery Exam
quizData.subtitle: PMDC standard evaluation on hydrocarbons, functional groups, and mechanisms.

questions.question: The conversion of an alkyl halide to an alkene by heating with alcoholic KOH is an example of:
questions.explanation: Alcoholic KOH acts as a strong base, abstracting a proton from the beta-carbon while the halide leaves, yielding an alkene.

questions.question: In an SN1 reaction mechanism, the rate-determining step involves:
options: Simultaneous nucleophile attack and leaving group departure (bimolecular)
questions.explanation: SN1 rate depends only on alkyl halide concentration (Rate = k[R-X]) during the slow heterolytic ionization to a carbocation.

questions.question: Lucas reagent used to differentiate 1°, 2°, and 3° alcohols consists of:
questions.explanation: Lucas test uses anhydrous ZnCl2 + conc. HCl; tertiary alcohols react immediately producing oily turbidity.

questions.question: Which functional group gives a silver mirror with Tollen's reagent?
questions.explanation: Aldehydes are easily oxidized to carboxylic acids, reducing Ag+ in Tollen's reagent to metallic silver.

questions.question: Saponification of triglycerides (fats) with NaOH produces:
options: Soap (sodium salts of fatty acids) and Glycerol
questions.explanation: Alkaline ester hydrolysis of fats cleaves the triester to yield glycerol (propane-1,2,3-triol) and sodium carboxylates (soap).

topics.title: 1.1 Projectile Trajectories & Newton's Laws
topics.readContent:
Module 3: Physics • Chapter 1

1.1 Projectile Trajectories & Newton's Laws

Independence of horizontal and vertical velocity components, maximum height (H = v0^2 sin^2 theta / 2g), time of flight, and maximum range at 45 degrees.

topics.title: Topic 1.1 Quick Quiz: Mechanics & Momentum Conservation

quizData.title: Mechanics & Projectiles Checkpoint Quiz
quizData.subtitle: 5 Rapid-Fire PMDC MCQs covering projectile ranges, momentum, and impulse

questions.question: At what angle of projection is the horizontal range of a projectile equal to its maximum height?
questions.explanation: Range R = 4 H / tan(theta). For R = H, tan(theta) = 4, so theta = arctan(4) ≈ 75.96°.

questions.question: In an elastic collision between two isolated bodies, which of the following quantities is conserved?
options: Both Linear Momentum and Kinetic Energy
questions.explanation: By definition, an ideal elastic collision conserves both total linear momentum and total mechanical kinetic energy.

questions.question: A force of 10 N acts on a body of mass 2 kg for 3 seconds. The impulse delivered to the body is:
questions.explanation: Impulse J = Force × time = 10 N × 3 s = 30 N·s (also equal to the change in linear momentum).

questions.question: The work done by a centripetal force on a particle moving with constant speed in a circular path is:
questions.explanation: Centripetal force is always perpendicular to instantaneous displacement vector (cos 90° = 0), so work done is zero.

questions.question: If the velocity of a moving car is doubled, its kinetic energy increases by a factor of:
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy KE = 1/2 m v^2. Doubling v quadruples (2^2 = 4) the kinetic energy.

quizData.title: Chapter 1: Mechanics & Work-Energy Comprehensive Exam
quizData.subtitle: PMDC standard evaluation on kinematics, laws of motion, and energy.

questions.question: A rocket works on the principle of conservation of:
questions.explanation: Rockets expel high-velocity exhaust gases backward; by Newton's 3rd law and linear momentum conservation, the rocket gains forward momentum.

questions.question: Escape velocity from the surface of Earth depends upon:
options: Mass of Earth and radius of Earth
questions.explanation: v_esc = sqrt(2 G M / R). It is independent of projectile mass or launch angle.

questions.question: The area under a Force-Displacement (F-d) graph represents:
questions.explanation: The integral of Force with respect to displacement integral(F dx) equals mechanical work done.

questions.question: A ball is thrown vertically upward. At the highest point of its trajectory, its:
options: Velocity is zero and acceleration is g downward
Velocity is zero and acceleration is zero
Velocity is maximum and acceleration is zero
Both velocity and acceleration are downward
questions.explanation: Instantaneous velocity passes through zero as it changes direction, while gravitational acceleration continues unabated at 9.8 m/s^2 downward.

topics.title: 1.1 Subject-Verb Agreement & Modifier Traps
topics.readContent:
Module 4: English • Chapter 1

1.1 Subject-Verb Agreement

Singular subjects connected by 'either...or' / 'neither...nor' take verbs agreeing with the closest subject. Collective nouns, intervening prepositional phrases, and indefinite pronouns.

resources.name: English Rules & PMDC Vocabulary List — PDF

topics.title: Topic 1.1 Quick Quiz: Sentence Correction Diagnostic

quizData.title: English Grammar Diagnostic Quiz
quizData.subtitle: 5 Rapid-Fire PMDC MCQs covering subject-verb agreement and error spotting

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence:
options: Neither the doctor nor the nurses were able to explain the anomalous ECG result.
Neither the doctor nor the nurses was able to explain the anomalous ECG result.
Neither the doctor or the nurses were able to explain the anomalous ECG result.
Neither the doctor nor the nurses are been able to explain the anomalous ECG result.
questions.explanation: When subjects are joined by 'neither...nor', the verb agrees in number with the closer subject ('nurses' is plural, requiring 'were').

questions.question: Identify the error: 'The team of medical specialists [A] have decided [B] to postpone [C] the clinical trial [D].'
questions.explanation: The true subject of the clause is the singular collective noun 'team' (not the plural 'specialists'), requiring singular 'has decided'.

questions.question: Select the correct conditional sentence:
options: If he had studied the histology slides, he would have passed the exam.
If he studied the histology slides, he would have passed the exam.
If he had studied the histology slides, he will pass the exam.
If he would study the histology slides, he passed the exam.
questions.explanation: Third conditional (past unreal condition) requires: If + past perfect (had studied), would have + past participle (would have passed).

questions.question: Choose the synonym for 'AMELIORATE':
questions.explanation: 'Ameliorate' means to make something bad or unsatisfactory better; to improve.

questions.question: Choose the antonym for 'BENIGN':
questions.explanation: In medical terminology, 'benign' refers to a non-cancerous/harmless condition; its exact antonym is 'malignant'.

quizData.title: Chapter 1: English Language Mastery Assessment
quizData.subtitle: PMDC standard evaluation on grammar, sentence correction, and vocabulary.

questions.question: Which word correctly completes: 'The surgeon was praised for her _____ handling of the delicate neurosurgical procedure.'
questions.explanation: 'Deft' means neatly skillful and quick in one's movements.

questions.question: Select the sentence with correct parallel structure:
options: The candidate likes reading medical journals, conducting lab experiments, and writing case reports.
The candidate likes reading medical journals, to conduct lab experiments, and writing case reports.
The candidate likes to read medical journals, conducting lab experiments, and write case reports.
The candidate likes reading medical journals, conduct lab experiments, and writing case reports.
questions.explanation: Parallelism requires consistent grammatical forms (here: all gerunds - reading, conducting, writing).

questions.question: 'EPHEMERAL' is closest in meaning to:
questions.explanation: 'Ephemeral' means lasting for a very short time.

questions.question: Choose the sentence with correct punctuation:
options: The patient had severe symptoms; however, the initial blood panel was unremarkable.
The patient had severe symptoms, however the initial blood panel was unremarkable.
The patient had severe symptoms; however the initial blood panel was unremarkable.
The patient had severe symptoms however; the initial blood panel was unremarkable.
questions.explanation: When linking two independent clauses with a conjunctive adverb like 'however', use a semicolon before and a comma after.

questions.question: Complete the analogy: STETHOSCOPE : PHYSICIAN :: SCALPEL : _____
questions.explanation: A stethoscope is the defining diagnostic tool of a physician; a scalpel is the defining operative tool of a surgeon.
